title: Closing search for per-key cache decay prior art
layman_summary: Searched production caching libraries and academic papers for any system that speeds up or slows down how fast a cache 'forgets' a specific item based on that item's own behavior, and found none that do this at the admission stage.
summary: A targeted, systematically-scoped search for prior art on admission-side cache mechanisms that vary the frequency-sketch decay/reset rate per individual key or key-segment, going beyond the hypothesis's existing five citations (TinyLFU, its cited aging/Hot-List related work, AdCache EDBT'26, ARC/LRU-K). The search checked two independent non-Java production ports of the TinyLFU admission mechanism at the source-code level (moka-rs/Rust, Mooncake's fak/Go clean-room derivative) and confirmed both use a single global periodic halving of the whole Count-Min sketch, structurally identical to Caffeine's own reference implementation. Caffeine's own GitHub issue tracker and design docs were checked for a per-key/per-segment decay proposal and none was found; its only adaptive-decay-adjacent work (a hill-climbed window-size knob) is globally tuned, the same class as AdCache already in the hypothesis's citations. The academic candidate most name-suggestive of the exact mechanism sought, OPODIS 2023's ALPS/ISketch paper, was fully read via fetch_grep (resolving an earlier OCR failure) and confirmed to reset all its sketches together on a fixed global frame boundary, with its per-item inter-arrival quantity used as an ML feature value rather than a decay rate -- this verifies rather than merely assumes the plan's pre-registered exclusion reason. Classical eviction-side aging (GDSF/Weighted-GDSF) and two recent (2024/2026) ML-admission and recency-frequency-adaptive systems (Baleen FAST'24, RFKV/vLLM-ARC arXiv 2026) were also checked and excluded on the pre-registered scope boundary (global constant, or eviction-side, or no admission filter at all). The overall result is a qualified negative: no mechanism was found that makes an individual key's admission-time frequency-sketch decay rate a function of that key's own observed behavior, across 2 verified source-level implementations, 1 production issue tracker, 6 sampled academic venues, roughly 13 distinct search queries, and 9 named candidate systems. The qualification matters: one candidate, STCCS ('Segmented Time Controlled Count-Min Sketch', ITU Kaleidoscope 2020), has a title that directly matches the search's exact boundary question but its full text could not be read with the available fetch tooling this pass, so it is held open rather than excluded; Baleen was found but not exhaustively verified for this specific claim either. The deliverable is written so the paper's related-work section can state 'to our knowledge, not found after a systematic search of X venues/Y queries/Z systems' while explicitly naming STCCS as an unresolved rather than silently-excluded candidate, which is more defensible to a reviewer than an unqualified novelty claim. A full comparison table (mechanism description, per-key vs global, driving signal, memory/hit-ratio figures where reported, venue/year) is provided in research_report.md for direct reuse in a related-work table.
answer:
A systematic search for admission-side caching mechanisms that vary a frequency-sketch's decay/reset RATE per individual key or key-segment (rather than by one global constant, one globally-tuned-but-uniform threshold, or an eviction-side policy) did not surface a mechanism closer to the hypothesis's claim than its existing five citations, with one candidate left genuinely unresolved.

On the industrial side: Caffeine's own wiki design pages contain no discussion of decay/aging/reset/segment mechanisms outside source code [1], and its GitHub issue tracker's closest matches (#504 'Variable refresh', #261 'Time-based Refresh') propose per-entry TTL expiration, a different mechanism from admission-sketch aging [4,5]. Two independent non-Java ports of the exact TinyLFU mechanism were verified at the source-code level: moka-rs's FrequencySketch performs a single global halving of every counter once the aggregate increment count crosses a fixed sample size, with code explicitly ported line-for-line from Caffeine [2]; Mooncake's clean-room `fak` derivative does the same over uint8 counters, per its own extensive design comments [3]. Neither varies per key. Caffeine's only genuinely adaptive-decay-adjacent mechanism, its hill-climbed admission-window size (commit b7fcda5, issue #1995), is a single globally-tuned knob driven by aggregate hit-density feedback -- the same class of mechanism as AdCache's RL tuning, already in the hypothesis's citation list [9,10].

On the academic side, the candidate most name-suggestive of the target mechanism, OPODIS 2023's ALPS/ISketch paper ('Sketching the Path to Efficiency'), was fully read via fetch_grep this pass (resolving a prior OCR failure). It is a meta-policy selector that resets all four of its sketches (Space-Saving, HyperLogLog, Count-Min, and a novel ISketch) together at fixed global frame boundaries; its per-item inter-arrival quantity (ISketch) is fed to an ML model as a feature value used to pick which whole heuristic policy to run next, not as a per-key decay rate on any sketch [6]. This confirms, rather than merely assumes, the exclusion reason the research plan pre-registered. Classical eviction-side aging (GDSF/Weighted-GDSF) uses a single global inflation clock and is eviction-side by design, excluded on two independent grounds [12,13]. Two recent systems -- Baleen (FAST'24, ML admission+prefetching for flash caches) and RFKV/vLLM-ARC (arXiv 2606.21238, 2026, recency/frequency-adaptive LLM KV-cache eviction) -- were checked; RFKV is confirmed eviction-side only, with no admission-time frequency filter at all (ARC has none) [14]; Baleen's exclusion is held at lower confidence since its full mechanism was not exhaustively grepped this pass [7].

One candidate is explicitly left unresolved rather than excluded: STCCS ('Segmented Time Controlled Count-Min Sketch', ITU Kaleidoscope 2020) has a title that directly matches the search's exact boundary question ('segmented' + 'time controlled' Count-Min sketch), but its full text was not reachable with the fetch tooling available this pass -- only an IoT-context abstract snippet was retrieved [15]. Given this, the negative result should be reported to the paper as qualified: 'not found after a systematic search of 2 verified source-level implementations, 1 production issue tracker, roughly 6 academic venues sampled, ~13 distinct queries, and 9 named candidate systems, with STCCS held open pending full-text access' -- not as an unqualified 'to our knowledge' claim. This preserves the rigor the hypothesis's existing five citations already show while being honest about the one gap a reviewer could otherwise find independently.

sources.title: Caffeine Design wiki
sources.summary: Fetched and fetch_grepped for decay/aging/reset/segment terms; zero matches -- the wiki's design prose does not separately document the TinyLFU aging mechanism, it lives only in source and the original 2017 paper.

sources.title: moka-rs FrequencySketch source
sources.summary: Verified at source level: single global periodic halving of every counter in the sketch when aggregate size crosses sample_size threshold, explicitly ported from Caffeine's Java implementation. No per-key variation.

sources.title: fak readmission.go (Mooncake clean-room derivative)
sources.summary: Extensively commented Go clean-room reimplementation of Mooncake's count_min_sketch.h admission gate; confirms identical global-halving-on-aggregate-threshold structure to Caffeine/moka, no per-key decay.

sources.title: Variable refresh (Caffeine issue #504)
sources.summary: Open feature request for per-entry variable TTL/refresh duration -- a different mechanism (expiration policy) from admission-sketch aging; excluded from scope.

sources.title: [Feature Request] Time-based Refresh
sources.summary: Closed issue, same TTL-refresh topic as #504; not an admission-sketch decay-rate proposal.

sources.title: Sketching the Path to Efficiency: Lightweight Learned Cache Replacement (OPODIS 2023)
sources.summary: Full text successfully read via fetch_grep this pass. ALPS is a meta-policy selector resetting 4 sketches together at fixed global frame boundaries; its ISketch tracks per-item inter-arrival time as an ML feature, not a per-key decay rate. Confirms plan's pre-registered exclusion reason.

sources.title: Baleen: ML Admission & Prefetching for Flash Caches (FAST'24)
sources.summary: Found via search; ML-based admission classifier for flash caches. Not exhaustively fetch_grepped for the specific decay-rate mechanism claim this pass -- tentative, lower-confidence exclusion, flagged as follow-up.

sources.title: HALP: Heuristic Aided Learned Preference Eviction Policy (NSDI'23)
sources.summary: Eviction-side preference-ranking ML policy for a YouTube CDN; not an admission-time frequency-sketch mechanism -- excluded as eviction-side by design.

sources.title: Adapt the window by hit density with starvation-guarded probes (Caffeine commit)
sources.summary: Caffeine's hill-climbed admission-window-size adaptation; a single global knob tuned by aggregate hit-density feedback, same class as AdCache's RL tuning already cited by the hypothesis.

sources.title: Feedback / Discussion: New hill climber for better hit rates
sources.summary: Discussion thread on Caffeine's window hill-climber; confirms it is a single global adaptive parameter, not per-key.

sources.title: [STORE] feat: Frequency admission + LRU lock optimization for local hot cache (Mooncake PR)
sources.summary: Adds a frequency-gated admission path to Mooncake's local hot cache; does not vary the underlying sketch's reset cadence per key.

sources.title: cache_rs::gdsf -- Greedy Dual-Size Frequency implementation
sources.summary: GDSF uses a single global inflation-clock (L-factor) aging term applied uniformly at eviction time; excluded as both global and eviction-side.

sources.title: Weighted Greedy Dual Size Frequency Based Caching Replacement Algorithm
sources.summary: Academic GDSF variant; same global inflation-clock aging structure, eviction-side, excluded on the same two grounds as [12].

sources.title: Recency/Frequency Adaptive KV Caching for Large Language Model Serving (arXiv 2606.21238, 2026)
sources.summary: Integrates ARC into vLLM for LLM KV-cache eviction; ARC has no admission-time frequency filter at all, so no decay-rate mechanism exists to compare -- excluded as out of scope by construction.

sources.title: STCCS: Segmented Time Controlled Count-Min Sketch (ITU Kaleidoscope 2020)
sources.summary: Title most directly matches the search's exact boundary question ('segmented' + 'time controlled' Count-Min sketch); only an IoT-context abstract snippet was retrievable this pass, full text unreachable with available tooling -- held OPEN, not excluded. Highest-priority follow-up.

sources.title: An improved data stream summary: the count-min sketch and its applications (Cormode & Muthukrishnan)
sources.summary: Canonical Count-Min sketch paper surfaced by scholarly search for sliding-window/decayed sketch variants; no per-item-decay-rate variant connected to cache admission was found in the returned result set.

follow_up_questions: STCCS (ITU Kaleidoscope 2020) could not be read in full this pass -- its title ('Segmented Time Controlled Count-Min Sketch') is the closest match found to the exact search boundary and must be read (via IEEE Xplore access or an alternative fetch route) before the negative-search claim can be considered fully closed.

Baleen (FAST'24) was found but not exhaustively fetch_grepped for whether its ML admission classifier's underlying frequency signal has any per-key decay-rate component; a targeted grep pass on the full PDF for 'decay', 'age', 'stale', 'window' would close this gap.

The streaming-algorithms literature descending from Cormode & Muthukrishnan's Count-Min sketch (sliding-window and exponentially-decayed sketch variants) is large and was only sampled with a handful of title-keyword scholarly queries; a deeper sweep specifically for per-item or per-class decay-constant variants (independent of any cache-admission framing) could surface a cross-applicable technique that a caching-systems-only search would miss.
